title: Dimension-preserving projective model of a strict localization
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $N\geq0$ be an integer such that every scheme-theoretic fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre] has topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] at most $N$. Let $x$ be a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point] of $X$, put $s=f(x)$ and $B=S_{(s)}$, and give $X_{(x)}$ its canonical map to $B$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit, lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality]. There exist a scheme $P$, a projective morphism $p:P\to B$ [def-pc-projective-morphism] which is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], a geometric point $y$ of $P$ over the closed point of $B$, and an isomorphism of $B$-schemes
$$\theta:X_{(x)}\xrightarrow{\sim}P_{(y)}.$$
Every scheme-theoretic fibre of $p$ has dimension at most $N$. Neither Noetherianity of $S$ nor finite presentation or quasi-compactness of $f$ is required.

source.place: Proposition 2.3, proof, printed p. 4 in the 28-page author version (the published IMRN version is cited as Proposition 3.1 by Illusie). Read online; local copy WANTED. First reduction paragraph (quasi-finite projection, Zariski main theorem, projective compactification).
